business_problem: DATEV needed to bridge mainframe and cloud-native software worlds so it could break monoliths into microservices, support cloud delivery, and avoid dedicating scarce staff to self-managing Kafka.
solution_summary: DATEV made Confluent Platform and Apache Kafka the integration layer between its legacy mainframe estate and a new cloud-native application portfolio spread across public and private clouds. As monolithic products were broken into microservices, Kafka became the asynchronous data hub that let separate application domains exchange events without tight coupling, while multi-datacenter replication bridged cloud-native and non-cloud-native environments. The platform underpins more than 100 microservice-based use cases and newer products such as cloud-based tax office management and invoice automation, where event-driven design speeds releases and keeps services scalable. Confluent's platform also gave developers self-service streaming capabilities and a supported operating model, reducing the resource burden of running Kafka alone. Together, these pieces turned streaming into a reusable modernization backbone for DATEV's broader digital-transformation program.

evidence_quotes: Using Confluent as the backbone of their new event-driven architecture, DATEV is accelerating its digital transformation journey, combining existing mainframe applications with newly developed applications across public and private clouds.
After weighing the options, DATEV decided on a data streaming architecture—based on Apache Kafka®—as an integrator and “bridge” between the two worlds.
With this strategy, DATEV can deliver its portfolio of applications directly to customers. Multi-datacenter replication is implemented as a connector between cloud-native and non-cloud-native worlds.
Now, there are over 100 microservice-based use cases across DATEV eG, which has helped deliver greater value to customers.
